findings.claim: Before this change, the stop after a failed stop returned its classification block with no error, because the refusal had been recorded at the failed stop. Now that next stop returns the block together with the refusal error (M15 stop 2 pins exactly this: a block plus an error naming -9.json). stopHookAnswer returns nil output whenever err != nil (engine/cmd/review_stop_hook.go:139), so the hook prints only the error and drops the block. `once` has already recorded the classify- keys, so that classification question is never shown in the session. This is the known -2 F1 loss, which L72 placed in T4w. T4o widens it to every stop that follows a failed pass while a refused file exists. Nothing in production calls WithClassified yet (the only non-test match is its definition, classify.go:35), so no live trigger reaches it today. T4w must handle this sequence, not only a first stop that carries a fresh refusal.

oneLine now writes every byte that is not a line break as it is, which resolves -5 F1 and the polisher finding. One side effect: lone C1 bytes such as 0x9B (CSI on 8-bit terminals), which T4n had turned into U+FFFD, now reach stderr raw again, beside ESC and the other C0 controls that already passed. The error text that carries them can be file names of refusals or git stderr. When verbose mode shows such a line, it can carry terminal control sequences. L74 records this as a risk it did not decide (ESC and other C0 controls) and no finding names it. Nothing here shows realistic input reaching it.
